alex_k: onboarding Liberta-13B (community fork) -> ran quick int4 conversion; cheap artifacts: output contains non-linguistic tokens and odd punctuation. suspect mismatch between exporter metadata and our loader + tokenizer id offsets.

maria_r: can you paste the exact conversion command and a short example of bad output?

alex_k: command: `python tools/convert_model.py --src liberta-13b.safetensors --dst redwood/liberta-13b --quant int4 --vocab-map vocab.json`
seeded prompt: "The quick brown fox"
fp16 ref: "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog"
int4 sample: "The quick brown fox  — %" (weird tokens inserted)

cheng_w: any warnings about rotary or KV cache shapes on load? sometimes head_dim metadata is wrong for community exports.

alex_k: loader logs: `rotary_head_dim: 32` but exporter header shows `rotary_head_dim: 64` in their README. also saw `embedding_size: 51200` vs our expected 51296 -> suspect token id shift.

jordan_t: if head_dim is wrong you get mismatched sin/cos application and QK decorrelation. that leads to fluent tokens being suppressed; combined with token-id shift it looks gibberish.

maria_r: try forcing rotary head dim and running a short determinism test. flags we added for previous forks: `--rotary-head-dim 64 --rotary-mode headwise`.

alex_k: forced to 64 -> fluency improved but still some tokens map wrong. I dumped token ids for first 10 tokens and compared to fp16 run: many token ids are off by +1 or -1 in ranges around punctuation/subtokens.

cheng_w: okay two parallel problems: (A) rotary head_dim misinterpretation, (B) tokenizer/model vocab id alignment. For (B) try a quick remap: `python tools/remap_vocab.py --in vocab.json --out vocab.remap.json --offset -1` and re-run.

alex_k: did remap -1 -> majority of common words align; perplexity on small eval dropped ~0.85. Still a few edge cases on rare unicode tokens.

maria_r: we should add converter-level checks: 1) assert rotary weight shapes consistent with reported head_dim, 2) compare top-1 token id histogram between tokenizer and model embedding matrix indices to detect bulk offsets. If mismatch, fail conversion or emit a warning.

jordan_t: +1. Also add an autodetect path: infer rotary_head_dim from state_dict shapes when present. If ambiguous, prompt user-supplied flag.

alex_k: opened PR in convertors: autodetect rotary_head_dim, assert rotary tensor shapes, run vocab-histogram check and emit a non-fatal error with suggested remap command. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/convertors/pull/315

ci-bot: CI: convertors/pr-315  onboard smoke tests: PASSED (3m 12s)

cheng_w: can we add an e2e sanity under tests/onboard/liberta/ that seeds generation and compares first-8 token ids and top-5 probs to fp16 baseline? tolerances: exact token ids for topk, probs within 0.01. This will catch both issues early.

alex_k: adding `tests/onboard/liberta/sanity_check.py` with fixtures: tokenizer.json, sample_fp16_topk.json, tiny int4 run with seed. Local bench: int4 p99 token latency ~24ms vs fp16 ~33ms on my dev-GPU.

maria_r: also update docs for exporters: require explicit rotary metadata and tokenizer normalization (we prefer NFC/NFKC) and note BOS/EOS index expectations. Add exporter-side warning when normalization differs.

jordan_t: once PR merges, push a small canary to staging and run our eval harness across 10 community forks to find other fragiles.

alex_k: will follow up with failing sample attachments and a short triage note in the PR. thanks team. :pray:
